classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Number fields, Dedekind ideals and finite linear algebra
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: Finite torsion-free modules over Dedekind domains are projective; nonzero fractional ideals are invertible; the field trace is nondegenerate and the codifferent is its integral dual. Smith reduction, elementary finite-dimensional linear algebra, completions and the Chinese remainder theorem are used. Integral symplectic bases exist for perfect alternating Z-forms.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: The actual nonfree lattice, exact trace-dual scalar, integral pseudobasis, center congruence ideals and exact phase are proved in PUN, rather than inferred from a commensurable replacement.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Hasse-Minkowski over a number field
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: A nondegenerate quadratic form over a number field is isotropic if it is isotropic over every completion.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: PUN1 handles square delta explicitly and complex completions automatically. PUN2 handles both t nonzero and a global isotropic vector at t=0, and local cancellation includes split algebras.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Original Host, Datum, Level and fixed Hermitian model
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: The actual Host, finite projective perfect alternating Datum, Level and each theorem printed fixed Hermitian-space hypotheses remain exactly as quantified. PUN does not construct the common field/host/Moduli family. The same Gm, xi0, embedding type and original lattices are retained.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: A supplied original FamilyUnif
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: PUN11 quantifies over the original supplied FamilyUnif and constructs all its ModelsOf/ModelBase/NegXi fields on the prescribed Hermitian space. It does not prove N1c.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Original all-family Data and CuspFD inputs
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: PUN12-PUN14 use every original Data, arbitrary component type, every rank and every CuspFD. Finite index is the original Gamma_index field; no normality or additional principal-level condition is assumed.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Exact supplied ModelBase for ExpoMatch
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: PUN17-PUN19 retain the literal model with its integral equivalence, trace pairing and exact original principal group, and A=1 for the final exponent theorem. This is the source expoMatch_models scope.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Complex tori, analytic coverings and tangent derivations
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: A full discrete lattice defines a compact complex torus; its quotient is the universal cover. Holomorphic additive maps are complex linear. Smooth-scheme tangent vectors are derivations or maps from dual numbers. Global holomorphic functions on a connected compact complex manifold are constant.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: PUN15 constructs the actual periods directly from the positive complex structure; PUN20 and PUN23 give the precise source tangent and integral-kernel dictionaries.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Riemann algebraicity and algebraic/analytic torus equivalence
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: A complex torus with a positive integral Riemann form is the analytification of an abelian variety; analytic homomorphisms between such tori are algebraic.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: The supplied IsPeriod gives the exact positive Hermitian form with imaginary part the original integral perfect B. PUN20 uses the resulting original torus and R-action; it does not appeal to a moduli-uniformization theorem.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Appell-Humbert classification and positivity
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: Hermitian-form/semicharacter factors classify holomorphic line bundles on a complex torus. The line is ample precisely when its Hermitian form is positive definite.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: PUN20 explicitly constructs alpha(Pa)=exp(pi i B(a,w0 a)), verifies the cocycle, symmetry, adjoint and primitive identities, and writes the normalized cubic cancellation. PUN21 computes the actual source commutator sign; PUN23 uses prim to identify the line itself.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: GAGA for the projective complex varieties used here
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: Analytification identifies coherent algebraic and analytic sheaves and their homomorphisms on a projective complex variety, and algebraizes the analytic maps between the projective varieties in use.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: Every application is to a constructed projective torus, its finite powers, a line bundle, its generators or a map of these varieties. No analytic relative theta-family or general nonproper algebraization theorem is inferred.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Dual abelian variety with universal Poincare bundle on all test schemes
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: The dual abelian variety represents the rigidified algebraically trivial line-bundle functor on every test scheme and commutes with field extension.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: PUN20 proves that the polarization map is an isomorphism using the perfect integral B. The original KTriv hypothesis gives a trivial translation class Zariski locally on Spec(A0), so its image in the represented functor is zero; the isomorphism forces x=0 for arbitrary, possibly nonreduced, C-algebras A0.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Global functions on a proper geometrically connected reduced variety
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: For a proper geometrically connected geometrically reduced variety over a field, global functions are the base field and this remains true after any field extension.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: PUN21 applies this only to the original constructed abelian variety after C -> k, so any two global generators differ by a scalar in k and the universal WeilIs condition follows.
